title: GATE 2026: M.Tech Admission, PSU Jobs & Exam Pattern
meta_description: GATE 2026 - Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering. PSU recruitment, M.Tech admission, salary ₹40-80K at PSUs, exam pattern Feb 7-15, and preparation strategy.

hero.one_liner: India's premier engineering entrance exam - gateway to M.Tech at IITs and direct recruitment to PSUs like ONGC, IOCL, NTPC, BHEL at ₹40-80K/month

what_is_it: GATE (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) is a national-level exam jointly conducted by IISc Bangalore and 7 IITs for testing comprehensive understanding of engineering/science subjects. GATE scores are used for: (1) M.Tech/M.E./PhD admission at IITs, NITs, IIITs, and other engineering colleges with MHRD fellowship of ₹12,400/month, (2) Direct recruitment to Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) like ONGC, IOCL, NTPC, BHEL, GAIL, PGCIL, BEL, etc., and (3) Some private companies also use GATE scores for recruitment.

The exam covers 30 subject papers including all major engineering branches (CSE, ECE, EE, ME, CE, CH), sciences (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Statistics), and newer additions (Biomedical, Environmental, Humanities). Each paper has 65 questions - a mix of MCQs and NAT (Numerical Answer Type) - to be solved in 3 hours for 100 marks.

GATE score is valid for 3 years. A good GATE rank (top 500-1000 depending on branch) opens doors to IIT M.Tech programs. For PSU recruitment, most PSUs set their own cutoff - typically GATE score of 500-700+ (out of 1000 normalized). PSU jobs through GATE offer ₹40,000-80,000/month starting salary with excellent perks.
GATE 2026 is organized by IIT Guwahati. The exam is held on 7, 8, 14, 15 February 2026 in two shifts (morning: 9:30 AM-12:30 PM, afternoon: 2:30 PM-5:30 PM) across 235 exam centers.

extra_sections.heading: GATE for PSU Jobs - How It Works
content: Many PSUs (Public Sector Undertakings) recruit engineers directly through GATE score instead of conducting their own exams. The process:
Step 1: Appear for GATE in your branch and get a valid score.
Step 2: When PSUs release recruitment notifications (typically April-August), apply with your GATE scorecard.
Step 3: PSUs shortlist candidates based on GATE score cutoff (varies by PSU and category).
Step 4: Shortlisted candidates appear for Group Discussion + Personal Interview conducted by the PSU.
Step 5: Final selection based on GATE score + GD/PI performance.
Major PSUs recruiting through GATE: ONGC, IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, GAIL, NTPC, PGCIL, BHEL, BEL, SAIL, NALCO, NHPC, MECL, MDL, HAL, and many more. Each PSU has different cutoffs and processes.
PSU salaries with GATE: Entry-level PSU engineer salaries range from ₹40,000-80,000/month including allowances. ONGC and IOCL are the highest-paying.
With perks (housing, medical, LTC, performance bonus), total compensation can reach ₹12-20 lakh/year at entry level.

extra_sections.heading: GATE Score vs Rank - What You Actually Need
content: GATE score is normalized across sessions and years, making direct mark comparison misleading. What matters is your GATE score (out of 1000) and All India Rank (AIR).
For IIT M.Tech admissions, you typically need AIR under 500-1000 depending on the branch and IIT.
For PSU recruitment (ONGC, IOCL, NTPC, BHEL, GAIL), GATE score cutoffs vary by company and category. General category cutoffs for top PSUs typically require a GATE score of 600-750.
Some PSUs like BARC have their own additional screening tests.
For IIT M.Tech: AIR 1-200 gets top IITs and branches. AIR 200-1000 gets other IITs/NITs with branch flexibility.
AIR 1000-5000 gets NITs and IIITs. Beyond 5000, options are limited to lower-ranked institutes.
Plan your score target based on your goal - PSU or M.Tech.

extra_sections.title: GATE score for top PSUs (general category)
extra_sections.desc: Top PSUs like ONGC and IOCL want roughly 600-750. IIT M.Tech needs an All India Rank under 500-1000.

extra_sections.heading: GATE for M.Tech - Is It Worth It?
content: M.Tech from IIT/NIT through GATE offers: (1) MHRD fellowship of ₹12,400/month for 2 years, (2) IIT brand value for placements, (3) Research exposure and specialization, (4) Higher starting salary - M.Tech from IIT commands ₹15-25 lakh/year in placements vs ₹6-12 lakh for B.Tech from non-IIT.
However, consider: You're spending 2 years in M.Tech (opportunity cost of 2 years' salary). If you can get a PSU job directly through GATE, that might be financially better in the short term.
M.Tech is better for: long-term career in R&D, academia, or product companies. PSU job is better for: stable career with good salary from day one.
Top M.Tech specializations by placement: CSE (AI/ML, Data Science) - ₹20-50 lakh placements at IITs. ECE (VLSI, Communication) - ₹12-25 lakh.
Mechanical/Civil - ₹8-15 lakh. Choose specialization based on industry demand, not just GATE score convenience.

extra_sections.heading: GATE for PSU jobs - the hidden opportunity
content: Over 200 PSUs accept GATE scores for direct recruitment - ONGC, IOCL, NTPC, BHEL, SAIL, GAIL, BPCL, HPCL, Power Grid, and many more. PSU starting salaries range from Rs 40,000-60,000/month with benefits including housing, medical, and pension.
Some PSUs like ONGC offer Rs 12-15 LPA for fresh GATE hires.
The GATE cutoff for PSU recruitment is generally lower than MTech at IITs. A score in the 500-600 range (out of 1000) can get you calls from multiple PSUs.
Many engineering graduates who don't want to do MTech take GATE specifically for PSU jobs - it's a well-paying, stable career with government benefits.

extra_sections.heading: Subject-wise preparation approach
content: Engineering Mathematics and General Aptitude carry 30 marks (out of 100) and are common across all branches. These are the easiest marks - linear algebra, calculus, probability, and verbal/numerical aptitude.
Master these first for guaranteed 20-25 marks.
Subject-specific papers carry 70 marks. Focus on the top 5-6 chapters that contribute 60-70% of questions.
For CS: algorithms, data structures, DBMS, OS, computer networks. For ME: thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, strength of materials.
For EE: power systems, control systems, electrical machines. Previous year analysis reveals the high-weightage topics clearly.
GATE 2026 added a new Energy Science section (XE-I) under the Engineering Sciences paper.
Foreign nationals can also appear, but only at exam centres inside India.

extra_sections.heading: Branch-wise PSU opportunities
extra_sections.content:
Mechanical: ONGC, BHEL, NTPC, IOCL, SAIL - maximum PSU vacancies. Electrical: Power Grid, NTPC, BHEL, NHPC.

Civil: NHAI, NHPC, WAPCOS. CS/IT: Limited PSU options (BSNL, ECIL) - most CS graduates prefer private sector.

Chemical: IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, GAIL. Decide your GATE branch based on PSU opportunities, not just BTech specialization.

extra_sections.heading: GATE 2026 exam details
extra_sections.content:
Conducted by one of the IITs (rotates annually). 65 questions in 3 hours.

Mix of MCQs (1 and 2 marks) and NAT (Numerical Answer Type - no options, type the answer). Negative marking: 1/3 for 1-mark MCQs, 2/3 for 2-mark MCQs.

No negative marking for NAT questions. Score normalized across sessions.

extra_sections.heading: Branch-wise preparation strategy
content: Different branches reward different focus. Master the 5 to 6 topics that carry most of your paper, then add breadth.
Previous year papers from 2010 to 2025 are free on the official GATE site, and the patterns repeat.

items.title: Computer Science (CS)
items.sub: DSA (15-20%), DBMS, OS, Computer Networks, Theory of Computation, Compiler Design, Digital Logic, Architecture.

items.title: Mechanical (ME)
items.sub: Thermodynamics and Fluid Mechanics together cross 30%. Plus SOM, Heat Transfer, Manufacturing, Machine Design.

items.title: Electrical (EE)
items.sub: Power Systems (15-18%), Control Systems, Machines, Network Theory, Electronics, Signals, EMT.

items.title: Civil (CE)
items.sub: Structural (RCC, Steel, Analysis, 25-30%), Geotech, Transportation, Environmental, Hydraulics, Surveying.

items.title: Electronics (EC)
items.sub: Analog, Digital, Signals and Systems, Control, Communication, EMT, VLSI. Network Theory overlaps with EE.

content: For CS, build DSA first and practise on LeetCode or GeeksforGeeks, since GATE increasingly tests algorithmic thinking.
ME is formula-heavy, so keep a formula sheet per subject and revise it daily.
For EE, Power Systems is the bread-and-butter topic for both the paper and PSU interviews.
EE has the widest PSU options: NTPC, Power Grid, BHEL, NHPC and state boards all hire through GATE.

extra_sections.heading: GATE preparation plan - 6 months
content: Month 1-2 (Foundation): Pick your top 5 high-weightage subjects. Study each from standard textbooks - not coaching notes.
For CS: Cormen (Algorithms), Galvin (OS), Navathe (DBMS). For ME: PK Nag (Thermodynamics), RK Rajput (Fluid Mechanics).
Solve GATE PYQs topic-wise after completing each chapter.
Month 3-4 (Practice): Complete remaining subjects. Start taking subject-wise mock tests.
Identify weak areas - the subjects where you score below 50% need revision. Join an online test series (GATE Academy, Made Easy, or IES Master - Rs 2,000-5,000 for full series).
Practice 30 GATE-level problems daily.

Month 5 (Mock intensive): Take 3 full-length mock tests per week. After each mock: analyze which questions you got wrong (conceptual error vs calculation error vs time management), track time spent per question, identify the 5 topics that cost you the most marks.
Revise those topics and retake similar questions.
Month 6 (Final revision): Take 1 mock test daily in the last 2 weeks. Revise formula sheets every morning.

Focus only on high-weightage topics - don't try to learn new topics this late. Engineering Mathematics and General Aptitude (30 marks combined) are the easiest to improve in the final month - revise linear algebra, calculus, probability, and verbal aptitude.
These 30 marks are often the difference between IIT admission and missing it.
For more details, see our guide on UGC NET 2026.
For more details, see our guide on JEE Main 2026.

extra_sections.heading: PSU recruitment through GATE
content: PSU hiring runs off your GATE score, not a separate exam.
Each company releases its own notification with a required paper and cutoff.

content: PSU interviews are heavily technical, drawn straight from your GATE subjects.
Expect questions like how a thermal power plant works (NTPC) or what load flow analysis is (Power Grid).
Notifications land at different times: ONGC around October to December, NTPC January to March, IOCL June to August.
For top PSUs you usually need a top 500 to 1000 rank, while second-tier and state PSUs call scores from 350 to 550, so apply everywhere.

extra_sections.heading: GATE marking scheme
content: Knowing the penalty changes how you guess.
MCQs carry negative marking, but MSQ and NAT questions do not.

items.title: MCQ (Multiple Choice)
items.sub: Four options, one correct. Carries negative marking of 1/3 or 2/3, so only guess when you can rule out two options.

items.title: MSQ (Multiple Select)
items.sub: One or more options can be correct. No negative marking, but you score only by picking every correct option and no wrong one.

items.title: NAT (Numerical Answer)
items.sub: No options at all. You type the value on an on-screen keypad. No negative marking, so always attempt these.

extra_sections.heading: GATE vs other engineering career paths
content: GATE MTech at IIT vs direct placement: An MTech from IIT adds 2 years to your career but increases starting salary by 30-50% for most branches. CS MTech from IIT graduates receive Rs 25-45 LPA offers vs Rs 8-15 LPA for BTech freshers.
For non-CS branches, the salary improvement is smaller (Rs 10-18 LPA vs Rs 5-8 LPA) but PSU eligibility and research opportunities open up.
GATE vs MBA: If you're an engineer considering MBA, compare carefully. MBA from IIM gives Rs 20-30 LPA starting but costs Rs 25-30 lakh in fees and opportunity cost.
GATE MTech from IIT costs Rs 2-3 lakh total with stipend of Rs 12,400/month. PSU job through GATE gives Rs 8-15 LPA with government benefits.
MBA makes sense for career changers; GATE makes sense for those who want to stay in engineering.

GATE for PhD and research: GATE qualifiers with high scores can pursue PhD at IITs and IISc with Rs 31,000-35,000/month fellowship (JRF). Research careers at ISRO, DRDO, BARC, and CSIR labs also recruit through GATE.
If you love your engineering subject and want to push boundaries, the research path offers intellectual satisfaction that corporate jobs rarely match.

extra_sections.heading: After the exam: scorecard and counselling
content: Your GATE 2026 scorecard is free to download until 31 May 2026, then ₹500 per paper until 31 December 2026.
M.Tech offers and PSU shortlisting run through COAP, the common portal where IITs and IISc publish seat allotments.

extra_sections.heading: Exam centres and paper choice
content: GATE 2026 is held in more than 200 cities, all within India.
You may attempt one or two papers, with the second chosen only from the allowed combinations.

extra_sections.heading: General Aptitude - free marks most students ignore
content: General Aptitude carries 15 marks - 5 questions of 1 mark (verbal ability) and 5 questions of 2 marks (numerical ability). These are the easiest marks in the entire GATE paper.
The questions test basic English comprehension, vocabulary, sentence completion, verbal analogies, logical reasoning, data interpretation, and elementary arithmetic.
Verbal Ability questions are at Class 10 English level. If you can read and understand a newspaper editorial, you can answer these without any preparation.
Common question types: sentence completion with appropriate words, identifying the correct meaning of a word in context, paragraph coherence, and critical reasoning (strengthen/weaken arguments).

Numerical Ability questions test basic math that you already know - percentages, profit-loss, time-work, permutation-combination, and data interpretation from simple graphs. These are significantly easier than your engineering mathematics questions.
A 10-minute revision of basic arithmetic formulas before the exam is sufficient preparation for this section.
Strategy: Attempt all 10 General Aptitude questions first - before touching your engineering paper. These 15 marks take 10-12 minutes and have nearly 100% accuracy for prepared candidates.
Starting with these easy marks builds confidence and settles exam nerves before you tackle the harder engineering questions.

extra_sections.heading: Common mistakes GATE aspirants make
content: A few avoidable mistakes cost more marks than weak concepts.
Fix these early.

items.title: Studying everything equally
items.sub: 5-6 subjects carry 70% of marks. Give them 70% of your time.

items.title: Skipping NAT practice
items.sub: No options, no partial marks. Practise numerical-answer questions separately.

items.title: Ignoring negative marking
items.sub: MCQs lose 1/3 or 2/3 per wrong answer. Only guess if you can rule out 2 options.

items.title: Not practising the virtual calculator
items.sub: Physical calculators are banned. Practise the on-screen one before exam day.

items.title: Starting too late
items.sub: A good score needs 6-8 months. Begin by July for the February exam.

extra_sections.heading: GATE coaching: which mode fits you

win.name: Online coaching
win.sub: Recorded lectures, tests and doubt sessions. Most toppers now study online. Best for working pros and remote students.

others.name: Self-study
others.sub: Textbooks, previous papers and NPTEL or YouTube. Best for disciplined students who already know 60%+ of the syllabus.

others.name: Offline coaching
others.sub: Classroom, printed material and peer group. Best if you need structure. Main hubs: Hyderabad and Delhi.

others.name: Test series (any mode)
others.sub: Matters more than the coaching itself. Simulates real GATE difficulty and flags weak areas.

extra_sections.text: GATE is the rare exam that keeps three doors open simultaneously - IIT M.Tech admissions, PSU jobs with ₹50,000+ starting salary, and direct PhD opportunities at premier research institutions.

preparation_tips: Focus 70% of preparation time on your core subject (85 marks) and 30% on General Aptitude (15 marks). Within the subject, identify high-weightage topics from previous year analysis - typically 3-4 topics contribute 40-50% of marks.
Previous year GATE papers (last 15-20 years) are the BEST resource. Many questions are repeated or follow the same pattern. Solve all previous year papers topic-wise first, then as full-length tests.

For PSU recruitment through GATE, you need a normalized score of 500-700+ (varies by PSU). For IIT M.Tech, you need to be in the top 1000-2000 (varies by branch). Set a target score based on your goal.

NAT (Numerical Answer Type) questions have no negative marking - these are free marks if you can solve them. Practice numerical problem-solving extensively. Even if you're not 100% sure of the answer, attempt all NAT questions.
Join a test series - practice 30+ full-length tests with timer. GATE time pressure is intense (1.5 minutes per question). Speed matters as much as accuracy.

faqs.question: What is the full form of GATE?
faqs.answer: GATE stands for Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering. It is a national qualifying exam for M.Tech admission and PSU recruitment, conducted by IIT Guwahati for the 2026 cycle.

faqs.question: Can non-engineering students take GATE?
faqs.answer:
Yes. GATE has papers in pure sciences (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Statistics), Life Sciences, Humanities, and other non-engineering subjects.

B.Sc./M.Sc. graduates can appear in their respective subject papers.

GATE in these subjects opens doors to M.Tech/PhD at IITs and research positions at labs like ISRO, DRDO, BARC.

faqs.question: I graduated 5 years ago. Can I still take GATE?
faqs.answer:
Yes. There is no age limit and no limit on the number of attempts.

You can appear for GATE any number of times. However, for M.Tech admission at IITs, some institutes have their own age criteria.

For PSU recruitment, age limits apply (typically 25-28 years for General category at most PSUs).

faqs.question: Which coaching is best for GATE?
faqs.answer:
Popular GATE coaching: Made Easy and The Gate Academy (offline), Unacademy and BYJU'S Exam Prep (online). However, many toppers have self-prepared using standard textbooks + previous year papers + test series.

A test series subscription (₹2,000-5,000) is more important than full coaching.

faqs.question: GATE CSE vs GATE ECE - which has more opportunities?
faqs.answer:
GATE CSE has the highest placement potential for M.Tech (₹20-50 lakh at IITs) but also the highest competition (100K+ candidates). GATE ECE has good PSU opportunities (ISRO, DRDO, BEL, ECIL) and decent M.Tech placements (₹12-25 lakh).

Both are excellent - choose based on your undergraduate branch and interest.

faqs.question: What is the difference between GATE and similar exams like CAT?
faqs.answer:
GATE is for engineering/science and focuses on technical depth. CAT is for MBA and tests general aptitude/business awareness.

The difficulty levels and competitive landscapes are different. If you're an engineer wanting to stay in tech, GATE (for M.Tech/PSU) is more relevant.

For management, CAT is the path.

faqs.question: Can I apply for both GATE and other exams simultaneously?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Many candidates prepare for GATE alongside UPSC (CSE for engineering services) or IBPS exams.

However, GATE preparation is rigorous. If you're serious about GATE, focus 80% on GATE and only use remaining time for other exams.

Trying to prepare equally for multiple exams often results in poor performance in all.

faqs.question: Is GATE only for engineering students?
faqs.answer:
No. GATE is open to Science graduates (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Statistics, Life Sciences), Architecture, and even Humanities (XH paper).

Science students can use GATE for MTech/PhD admissions and PSU recruitment in research roles at CSIR, DRDO, ISRO, and BARC.

faqs.question: How many years is GATE score valid?
faqs.answer:
GATE score is valid for 3 years from the date of result announcement. You can use a single GATE score for multiple PSU applications and MTech admissions over 3 years.

If your score improves in a later attempt, you can use the better score.

faqs.question: What GATE rank is needed for IIT MTech?
faqs.answer:
Top IITs (Bombay, Delhi, Madras, Kanpur): GATE rank under 200-500 for popular branches (CS, EE). Less popular branches: rank 500-2000.

Second-tier IITs and NITs: rank 1000-5000. The exact cutoff depends on branch, category, and year.

A GATE score of 700+ (out of 1000) typically gets calls from multiple IITs.

faqs.question: Is there an age limit for GATE?
faqs.answer: No. There is no age limit for GATE, and no cap on the number of attempts. Anyone who meets the educational eligibility can appear, at any age.

faqs.question: How many questions and marks are there in GATE?
faqs.answer: Each GATE paper has 65 questions for 100 marks, in a 3-hour computer-based test. General Aptitude carries 15 marks and the subject section carries 85.

faqs.question: Is a calculator allowed in the GATE exam?
faqs.answer: No physical calculator is allowed. GATE provides an on-screen virtual scientific calculator, so practise with it before exam day.

faqs.question: How many times is GATE held in a year?
faqs.answer: GATE is held once a year, usually in February. The score then stays valid for three years.
